title: Honest Interval Length Relative to Design Standard Deviation in Balanced Bipartite Experiments
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal below novelty floor: tier=subfield < floor=field and NOT salvageable in scope; independent MAIN validity confirms sound specialized matched sqrt(D) interval theorem with no bounded same-scope field repair.
gap_reasons: Significance remains confined to exactly balanced, distinct-pair experiments with n=m/2: the degree-cap supremum does not characterize the price for an individual public graph or demonstrate precision consequences on the consumer’s network.
The coarse Chebyshev construction provides order attainment without an operational assessment of its conservativeness
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived the full finite-size sqrt(D) honest-interval/actual-SD order with a total observable attainer, an all-Borel independently randomized complete-record lower bound, and a sufficient uniform Gaussian regime. The math review passes with ten discovery-proved statements and two verified-attested cited sources, but the cold novelty referee and independent MAIN validity consult rate the specialized balanced distinct-pair package subfield below the unchanged field floor. No formalization or Lean certification was attempted; editorial status/comparator issues and absent presolve enumeration receipts remain disclosed rather than silently repaired.
tldr: Exactly balanced intervention assignment identifies the all-treated versus all-control effect, but one trial reveals only one entry of each response table. The focal question determines the matched finite-design order of \(J_m(D)\), the worst-case expected length of any uniformly honest original-record interval divided by the actual standard deviation of the endpoint estimator. A graph-only interval supplies an upper benchmark. The converse must retain distinct pairs, mixed factual responses, independent procedure randomization, and the stipulated variance floor on the entire class. A separate sufficient Gaussian regime tests whether reliable oracle normal approximation can coexist with a diverging price for feasible honesty.
gap: Sharp covariance bounds and nonlearning results characterize important components of uncertainty, but the verified results do not evaluate all connected honest intervals by the table-specific actual design standard deviation in this balanced distinct-pair experiment.
fill: A matched finite-design characterization, a total original-record attaining interval, and an unrestricted honest-interval converse answer that decision problem. Supporting Gaussian separation isolates uncertainty about precision from failure of normal approximation.
